cards.text: This psalm kicks off with a party: "Hallelujah! Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever." Then the writer has some history to tell, and friend, it's an HONEST one.

cards.question: The writer asks who can describe the mighty acts of the LORD or fully proclaim His praise. What's he getting at?

cards.text: Then he says who's blessed: those who uphold justice and practice righteousness at all times. At ALL times, friend. Not just when somebody's watching the cookie box.
Now he gets personal. He asks the LORD to remember him and to visit him with His salvation.

cards.question: True or false: the writer wants the LORD's salvation so he can rejoice along with God's people.

cards.text: Then the music drops. He confesses: "We have sinned like our fathers; we have done wrong and acted wickedly." No excuses! I once blamed a lopsided cookie on the oven for a WEEK. The oven was fine. It was me.

cards.question: The writer starts with Israel's fathers back in Egypt, who saw God's wonders up close. True or false: they understood those wonders and remembered His kindness.
Fresh out of Egypt, where does the psalm say Israel's fathers rebel?

cards.text: So they rebel right there by the sea. You'd think God drops them on the spot. NOPE. He saves them anyway.

cards.question: God saved them anyway, for the sake of His name and to make His ___ known.

cards.text: He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up, and He led them through the depths as through a desert. The DEPTHS. Dry. I can't even keep the counter dry when somebody rinses a mixing bowl.

cards.question: God saves Israel from the enemy that hated them, and the waters come back over that enemy. True or false: a few of the enemy make it out.
Their enemies are gone. How do the people respond right then?

answers.text: They believe and sing His praise
They ask to go back to Egypt
They build an altar of stones

cards.text: Happy ending? Not yet. "Yet they soon forgot His works and failed to wait for His counsel." I walk into the pantry and forget the sprinkles. These folks walked out of a SEA and forgot that.

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, they craved intensely and ___ God in the desert.
God gives the people what they asked for in the wilderness. What does He send along with it?

cards.text: Back in the camp, jealousy moves in. I know that look, friend. I gave it to a shiny new stamper once.

cards.question: In the camp in the wilderness, who do the people envy?

cards.text: That's Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, the holy one of the LORD. Two men in this mess are Dathan and Abiram, who rose up against Moses (Numbers 16:1-2).

cards.question: True or false: when the earth opens up under the rebels, Dathan gets away.

cards.text: The earth swallowed Dathan and covered Abiram's group. Then fire blazed through their company, and flames consumed the wicked.

cards.question: Next, at Horeb, the people make a molten image and worship it. What is it?

cards.text: The psalm says they exchanged their Glory for the image of a grass-eating ox. That's like trading my whole bakery for one crumb. And the crumb can't bake. The crumb can't do ANYTHING. It's a CRUMB.

cards.question: At Horeb, they ___ God their Savior, who did great things in Egypt.

cards.text: This is the God of wondrous works in the land of Ham and awesome deeds by the Red Sea. So He said He would destroy them.

cards.question: Someone stood before God in the breach to turn His wrath away from destroying the people. Who?
Next, the psalm turns to the pleasant land and to God's promise. True or false: the people believed His promise.

cards.text: They despised the pleasant land. They grumbled in their tents and didn't listen to the voice of the LORD. Grumbling in the tent? That's the group chat the boss isn't in.

cards.question: So the LORD raises His hand and swears an oath about the grumbling people. What does He swear?

answers.text: To cast them down in the wilderness
To lead them straight into the land
To give them a king like the nations

cards.text: He also swore to scatter their offspring among the nations. Keep that one in your apron pocket, friend.
Then they yoked themselves to Baal of Peor, a false god (Numbers 25:3). They ate sacrifices offered to lifeless gods.

cards.question: They provoked the LORD to anger with their deeds, and a ___ broke out among them.

cards.text: Then one man stands up: Phinehas, Aaron's grandson (Numbers 25:11). He steps right in.

cards.question: True or false: when Phinehas stood and intervened, the plague was restrained.
What Phinehas did was credited to him as ___ for endless generations to come.

cards.text: Next, the waters of Meribah. They angered the LORD there, and trouble came to Moses because of them.

cards.question: At the waters of Meribah, the people rebelled against His Spirit. What does Moses do?

cards.text: Then they get into the land. The LORD had commanded them to destroy the peoples there. They didn't.

cards.question: Instead of destroying the peoples in the land, what does Israel do with those nations?
Israel worshiped the idols of those nations, and the idols became a ___ to them.

cards.text: Then comes the darkest line in the psalm. They sacrificed their sons and daughters to the idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with blood.
No softening it, friend. The psalm says they defiled themselves by their actions and prostituted themselves by their deeds.

cards.question: True or false: after all Israel has done, the LORD lets it go without anger.
He delivered them into the hand of the nations, and those who ___ them ruled over them.

cards.text: Their enemies oppressed them and subdued them under their hand. Remember the sea that swallowed their enemies? Now the enemies are on top.

Many times He rescued them, but they were bent on rebellion and sank down in their iniquity. That's like getting rescued from a stuck elevator, then pushing the button for that SAME elevator. And friend, I'd do it. I would ABSOLUTELY do it.

cards.question: Israel keeps rebelling and sinks down in iniquity. Then they cry out in distress. What does God do?

answers.text: He sends them a new law

cards.question: God hears Israel's cry and relents. What does the psalm say He remembers?

cards.text: He relented by the abundance of His loving devotion. That's the same loving devotion from the very first line of this psalm. Still there. Still enduring.

cards.question: True or false: the people who held Israel captive showed them no compassion at all.

cards.text: Then the writer turns all of this history into his own prayer.

cards.question: The writer asks the LORD to save His people and gather them from the nations. Why does he want them gathered?

answers.text: So they can give thanks to His name
So they can defeat their enemies
So they can take back their land

cards.text: He closes: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting." Then he tells all the people to say amen, and ends right where he started: "Hallelujah!" Go ahead, baker, say it. Mine comes out a little muffled through the mustache, but it COUNTS.

findings.problem: "I gave it to a shiny new stamper once" adds something new to his backstory. The backstory never says he gave the replacement stamper a jealous look. The joke also calls back to the new stamper, and nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up. The card also has 3 sentences.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
